messages:
devon: FYI seeing oddness on prod during a capacity blip — circuit breaker trips but requests keep hitting the heavy model for ~200ms before finally failing. clients see long tails.
kevin: ugh. any chance the route override header isn't making it through the gateway? which header are we using for downshift now?
sophia: we use `x-rw-route-mode: degrade` in the rollout branch. gateway should convert that into a routing decision to pick `model:small` variant.
maya: logging from the gateway shows the header present on ingress but the router logs don't show the override path being taken. snippet: ```INFO route_matcher: matched default_lane; headers={x-rw-route-mode: degrade}``` then later ```INFO model_selector: selected model=redwood-13b-full```
devon: exact. looks like matcher sees header but the route priority evaluation is ignoring lane overrides when capacityScore < 0.2 — suspect short-circuit in the priority function.
kevin: can someone paste the prioritized-routing pseudocode? I can try a quick fix.
sophia: from memory: ```if capacity < threshold and circuit_open: select(next_highest_priority) else select(primary)``` — note that `next_highest_priority` is computed from static weights, not header overrides.
ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-479 (routing-degrade-header-bypassed) — alerted on 1795123010.
kevin: ahhh. so header-driven lanes are only applied during normal matching, not the CB path. we should treat header overrides as higher precedence than capacity fallback.
maya: agree. quick patch idea: move header-lane resolution to before circuit-breaker evaluation and tag the request with `route_hint`. then CB can consult `route_hint` when calculating fallback targets.
devon: sound plan. any telemetry we should add to ensure we don't regress? want per-request `route_hint` in traces + metric for "forced_degrade_miss" when header present but override wasn't applied.
sophia: +1. also add a boolean counter for `override_respected` and a histogram of time-to-decision for routing (so we can see if extra lookups add latency).
kevin: I'll open a tiny PR to reorder the steps and add the counters. will also add a console flag behind `rollout.feature.headerBasedRoutingFix` so we can toggle.
devon: please include a brief migration note for Dedicated customers — some have custom gateways that strip unknown headers. might need to map header to `x-forwarded-rw-route` at ingress.
kevin: good catch. I'll add a note and a small document in the console docs.
sophia: one more: when header requests are forced to the cheaper model, we should emit a log line `route_override_applied` with `model` and `requested_model` so cost accounting can attribute correctly.
maya: deploying a canary of the reorder to staging now (1795123030).
infra-bot: deploy start: canary/routing-reorder@kevin -> staging (pods=3).
infra-bot: deploy success: canary/routing-reorder@kevin -> staging (1795123042).
devon: after staging smoke looks good, let's roll to prod with 10% rollout + 3m evaluation. ops: ready for manual rollback if we see any spike?
ops-bot: standby for rollback window 3m after rollout start. will alert on error-rate > 0.5% or latency p90 > 30ms.
kevin: PR link: https://git.redwood.ai/p/routing-reorder/compare — includes tests and new metrics. starting prod rollout now. (1795123045)
sophia: awesome. thanks team. :thumbsup:
